detail.longDescription: I made this script: val = 0xF81F mask = 0xFF final = val & mask print(f"Original: {val:#04x}") print(f"MASK: {mask:#04x}") print(f"FINAL: {final:#04x}") and I got: Original: 0xf81f MASK: 0xff FINAL: 0x1f As you can see my value is 16 bit while my mask is 8 bit. Does Python pad with 0 when necessary or internally stores integers into a fixed size initialized with 0? How was it determined that the mask would be applied on the last 8 bits of my value instead of the first 8 bits?
